oneTimers: Costs tied to the July 19 Incident and related matters were $18.1M in the quarter (mostly inside G&A), down from $39.7M a year ago.
Stock-based compensation and related payroll taxes were $317.6M — the main reason non-GAAP net income attributable to CrowdStrike ($283.4M) is about 10× the GAAP attributable figure ($27.8M).
$18.2M of the quarter's $46.0M consolidated net income belonged to a non-controlling interest; net income attributable to CrowdStrike was $27.8M.
otherDetail: Interest and other items netted +$69.7M: $40.5M of interest income and $35.2M of other income, net (including $36.4M of gains on strategic investments), less $6.1M of interest expense.

segments.name: Subscription
segments.note: The Falcon security platform, sold by subscription — 95% of all revenue.

segments.name: Professional services
segments.note: Security experts for hire — incident response and setup help.

takeaways.text: Annual recurring revenue grew 24% to $5.51B, with $255.8M of net new ARR added in the quarter — demand for the Falcon platform stayed strong.
takeaways.title: ARR keeps compounding

takeaways.text: The operating loss narrowed to $30.6M from $118.7M a year ago; interest and investment gains of $69.7M, plus a $6.9M tax benefit, turned the quarter profitable overall.
takeaways.title: Operating loss shrank fast

takeaways.text: Free cash flow was $468.5M on $590.9M of operating cash flow — CrowdStrike's cash generation is far stronger than its GAAP profit suggests.
takeaways.title: Cash flow tells another story

verdict: CrowdStrike grew revenue 26% to $1.39B and cut its operating loss to $31M; investment gains and a tax benefit turned that into a $46M net profit.
